data.name: Jabran
data.gender_notes: Jabran is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jabran means great, mighty, powerful and strong. It is a name that conveys a sense of strength and courage. The name Jabran carries the meaning “Great, Mighty” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jabran usually hope their child will grow to embody great, mighty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Jabran is a name that is rooted in the spiritual tradition of Islam. It is believed to be a name that is bestowed upon those who have great inner strength and the ability to overcome adversity.
data.etymology: Jabran belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Great, Mighty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jabran total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

People with this name are often regarded as being brave, fearless, and powerful individuals, who are unafraid to face challenges head-on. In the Islamic society, strength and courage are highly valued qualities, and a name like Jabran would instill a sense of respect and admiration from those around the individual. Since Jabran is a name that evokes images of strength and power, it is not uncommon to find individuals with this name in leadership roles in Islamic societies.

According to Islamic teachings, true strength comes from inner peace and submission to the will of Allah. Therefore, Jabran, as a name, serves as a reminder to continuously strive towards this inner strength and to remember that true power lies in one's connection to Allah. By embracing themeaning of the name and using it as a source of inspiration, an individual can seek to embody the divine traits of power, strength, and courage in their daily life, which is a valuable spiritual goal in Islam.
